**Width changes the scale of computation and gradients unless the parameterization compensates.** A learning rate that produces sensible feature updates in a narrow network can cause updates to vanish or explode as hidden width grows. Maximal-update parameterization coordinates scaling rules so updates remain meaningful across compatible widths. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03466)

This makes a small model a more useful proxy for tuning a larger member of the same family. The benefit is not merely copying one number; initialization, layer roles, optimizer settings, and learning-rate scaling must all follow the intended scheme.

**Width transfer is not arbitrary model transfer.** Moving from 40M to 70B parameters may also change depth, architecture, data mix, batch size, and training duration. Those differences can invalidate the proxy even if width scaling is correct.

Check activation and update behavior across several small widths, then run limited large-model sanity checks before spending the full budget. Report which hyperparameters transferred and which still needed adjustment. MuP can reduce a costly tuning problem under its assumptions; it does not certify that any small model's exact optimum will remain optimal at any larger scale.

**Technical details and references.**

Maximal-update parameterization scales initialization, learning rates, and related quantities with width so feature updates remain meaningful as width changes. Under a compatible model family, this can make useful hyperparameters transfer from smaller proxies. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03466)

It is not a guarantee that an arbitrary 40M model's exact optimum transfers to an arbitrary 70B model. Depth, architecture, data, batch size, training duration, optimizer details, and finite-width effects can invalidate the comparison. Apply the parameterization consistently to input, hidden, and output layers and verify coordinate/update behavior.

Run small width-scaling tests and limited large-model sanity checks before committing the full budget. Report the transfer domain and residual tuning rather than presenting proxy tuning as a universal zero-risk shortcut.
